step_logs.text: Any sign of head or neck injury?

Check AIRWAY, BREATHING, CIRCULATION (ABCs). Start timing the duration of the convulsions. Place an intravenous (i.v.) line if possible. Ensure the person is in a safe place. Do not leave the person alone. Do not put anything in the mouth. For a person with possible head injury, neuroinfection, or focal deficits, refer urgently to hospital.
SPECIAL POPULATION: Is the woman in the second half of pregnancy OR up to 1 week post partum AND has no past history of epilepsy?

Give medication to stop convulsions. If no i.v. established: give diazepam rectally or midazolam buccally/intranasally. If i.v. established: start normal saline, glucose, and give emergency medication (diazepam or lorazepam i.v.).
Have the convulsions stopped within 10 minutes of 1st dose of emergency medication?
Has the person had convulsive movements lasting longer than 1-2 minutes?

Has the person had at least 2 of the following symptoms during the episode(s): loss of consciousness/impaired consciousness, stiffness/rigidity, bitten tongue/injury, incontinence, or post-convulsion fatigue/confusion/headache?
Is there an acute cause? (e.g., neuroinfection, fever, head injury, metabolic abnormality, intoxication/withdrawal)
Does the person have epilepsy? Has the person had at least two seizures on two different days in the past year?
Assess for underlying cause via physical/neurologic examination. Are any of the following present: Birth asphyxia or trauma, head injury, brain infection, or family history of seizures?

PROTOCOL 1: Provide psychoeducation to the person and carers. Promote functioning in daily activities. Initiate antiepileptic medications (e.g., Carbamazepine, Phenobarbital, Phenytoin, or Sodium Valproate) starting at the lowest dose and increasing slowly. For women of childbearing age: advise folate (5 mg/day) and avoid valproate. For people living with HIV: check drug interactions, valproate preferred. Follow-up every 3-6 months: evaluate side-effects, review adherence, and review psychosocial interventions. If the person has no >50% reduction in convulsions, increase the dose to maximal tolerated or switch medication. If the person has been convulsion-free for several years, consider gradual discontinuation over 2 months while monitoring closely.
Exit: End of Epilepsy Management Protocol.

Suspect CONVULSIVE SEIZURES

Suspect EPILEPSY

EPILEPSY is likely

If there is imminent risk of suicide, assess and manage before continuing to Protocol 1.
Has the person attempted a medically serious act of self-harm? (Check for signs of poisoning/intoxication, bleeding from self-inflicted wound, loss of consciousness, or extreme lethargy)

Is there an imminent risk of self-harm/suicide? (Current thoughts/plan of self-harm/suicide, or history of thoughts/plan in the past month or act in the past year in a person who is now extremely agitated, violent, distressed or lacks communication)
IMMINENT RISK OF SELF-HARM/SUICIDE is likely.

PROTOCOL 2: Imminent risk of self-harm/suicide. Remove means of self-harm/suicide. Create a secure environment and DO NOT leave the person alone. Supervise to ensure safety at all times. Attend to mental state. Provide psychoeducation, psychosocial, and carers support. Follow-up: maintain regular contact, decrease contact as person improves, or increase intensity and refer if not improving.
Does the person have concurrent MNS conditions? (Depression, Disorders due to substance use, Child & adolescent mental and behavioral disorders, Psychoses, Epilepsy)
Manage the concurrent conditions. See relevant modules.
Does the person have chronic pain?

Does the person have emotional symptoms severe enough to warrant clinical management? (Difficulty carrying out usual activities, repeated self-medication for emotional distress, unexplained physical symptoms, marked distress or repeated help-seeking)

Follow-up for as long as the risk of self-harm/suicide persists. Maintain regular contact. Assess for improvement; decrease contact as the person improves, or increase intensity/duration and refer to specialist if not improving.
End of Self-Harm / Suicide Assessment and Management.
